trust_decision.summary: Whether a remote peer may add topics to its per-peer topic set (connected_peer.topics, plus topic metrics): via SUBSCRIBE it passes the configured TopicSubscriptionFilter (default AllowAll, so no cap), and via GRAFT the pinned code inserts every grafted topic with no check at all.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'GRAFT topics unbounded growth'; handle_graft is the obvious target, and its first loop inserts every grafted topic into connected_peer.topics.

remote GRAFT -> handle_graft (fix inserts a 'peer not subscribed -> drop, no PX' check after the backoff penalty and before the mesh_n_high check; fix.diff:117-123)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:264 together with protocols/gossipsub/src/subscription_filter.rs:107-159 (the default filter type changes from AllowAllSubscriptionFilter to MaxCountSubscriptionFilter<AllowAll> with a new Default impl)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about GRAFT, and the SUBSCRIBE path already has a pluggable filter (MaxCountSubscriptionFilter exists, subscription_filter.rs:107-159), so a solver can argue that capping subscriptions is the application's configuration choice, not a bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A peer that sends SUBSCRIBE and GRAFT for a topic we joined must still be meshed. SUBSCRIBE is processed before control messages in the same RPC (behaviour.rs:3284-3285 before 3391), and the existing tests rely on that. A GRAFT during backoff must still be penalised (the changelog explicitly keeps this; fix.diff:39-41). An over-broad fix that drops all GRAFTs from peers lacking a recorded topic before the backoff check, or rejects GRAFT for joined topics, breaks meshing or loses the penalty. A too-low default cap would reject legitimate SUBSCRIBE RPCs, because the filter's Err drops the whole RPC's subscriptions (behaviour.rs:1954-1961).

O6_input_shapes: GRAFT for a topic the local node has not joined (already ignored for mesh at behaviour.rs:1520-1530, but the topic was still recorded at 1391-1398)
GRAFT for a topic the local node joined but the peer never SUBSCRIBEd to
many distinct topics in one SUBSCRIBE RPC (max_subscriptions_per_request, subscription_filter.rs:124)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A PRUNE for any topic, including one never joined, always records a (topic, peer) backoff entry, so the per-topic backoffs map grows with remote-chosen topics; the fix did not touch it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Entries expire via the heartbeat (backoff.rs:154-178), and the remote backoff is capped at 3600 s (behaviour.rs:88,1590), so a solver can call it already bounded and a different structure from per-peer topics.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point (behaviour.rs), with the sink in protocols/gossipsub/src/backoff.rs:96 via remove_peer_from_mesh(.., always_update_backoff=true) at behaviour.rs:1587-1596

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It mirrors the removed GRAFT reasoning ('if a peer prunes us it must have been subscribed'), the same comment style as behaviour.rs:1389-1390.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: IHAVE implies the peer is subscribed to the topic, so a maintainer could plausibly record it for gossip targeting.
